summary: This bill prohibits imposing or carrying out any federal death sentence after enactment and requires resentencing of all persons sentenced to death before that date.

scores.thoughts: The bill prohibits the federal death penalty and requires resentencing for existing cases. It contains no provisions related to government budgets, appropriations, or expenditures. Any potential minor administrative cost savings from eliminating death penalty proceedings are speculative and not addressed in the text.
The bill makes no reference to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection. It is exclusively focused on criminal sentencing.
No provisions in the bill address healthcare policy, insurance, public health programs, or medical services.
The legislation does not mention firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains nothing related to immigration enforcement, visas, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No content in the bill pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not address military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces matters.
There are no environmental regulations, climate provisions, or energy policy elements in the legislation.
The bill makes no changes to welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other social safety net policies.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
The legislation does not address drug criminalization, decriminalization, or enforcement priorities.

The entire bill is devoted to abolishing the federal death penalty and requiring resentencing of existing death row inmates. This constitutes a direct reform of federal criminal sentencing practices by eliminating the harshest available penalty, aligning with the reform and rehabilitation end of the spectrum rather than tougher sentencing.
The bill contains no trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
No fiscal policy, deficit, or debt-related measures are present.
The legislation does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign aid, international assistance, or diplomatic funding provisions exist in the bill.
The bill does not touch on voting rights, election procedures, or voter access.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions are included.
The bill makes no reference to labor law, unions, worker protections, or employment policy.
There are no provisions concerning religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
